children.name: Pseudaneitea aspera Burton, 1963
children.description:
External: Usually black; 19 lateral grooves (most unbranched) on each side of dorsum; fine, dense papillae on skin; anus near perinotum and without pre-anal groove (Burton 1980).

Internal: Jaw with long central plate and median cusp level with wingtips; straight, short oviduct; round, twisted ball of tubular oviduct gland at mid-point of oviduct; spermatheca attached at anterior end of oviduct; relatively short penis (Burton 1980).

Has a reproductive system similar to those of Reflectopallium pseudophyllum and P. dendyi, to which it may be closely related (Burton 1980).

children.name: Pseudaneitea multistriata Burton, 1963
children.description:
External: 22 lateral grooves (about half branching) on each side of dorsum, with 13 grooves after the mantle; many conical papillae on dorsum; pre- and post-anal grooves present (Burton 1980).

Internal: Jaw with a central plate length 2.25x its width, a strong medial cusp, and short, rounded wings; wide, straight, muscular, fairly long oviduct; very long penis with a narrow, twisted apical end widening suddenly at half its length (Burton 1980).

children.name: Pseudaneitea nodosa Burton, 1977
children.description:
External: 20-22 lateral grooves (most bifurcating) on each side of the dorsum; low, round papillae in skin; anus near perinotum and without anal groove (Burton 1980).

Internal: Long, muscular, curving oviduct with a round, tubular oviductal gland at its posterior end; round spermatheca with thin duct attached at halfway point along oviduct (Burton 1980).

Externally similar to P. multistriata (Burton 1980).

children.name: Pseudaneitea powelli Burton, 1963
children.description:
External: Gray body with two longitudinal lines of dark gray spots on each side of dorsum; 19 lateral grooves (some bifurcated) on each side of dorsum; low, round papillae; anus with a pre-anal groove and near perinotum (Burton 1980).

Internal: Jaw with wide central plate and a median cusp that extends below the wingtips; short oviduct with oviductal gland on posterior end; spermatheca with a thick duct attached at mid-point of oviduct (Burton 1980).

children.name: Pseudaneitea pseudophyllum
children.description: Pseudaneitea pseudophyllum is a species of air-breathing land slug, specifically a leaf-veined slug, a terrestrial pulmonate gastropod mollusc in the family Athoracophoridae.

children.name: Pseudaneitea ramsayi Climo, 1973
children.description:
External: Black body; 25-25 grooves (few branched) on either side of body; fine, dense papillae on skin; anus between mantle and perinotum on a right lateral groove (Burton 1980).

Internal: Yellow albumin gland; male and female ducts combined into a hermaphrodite duct; long, muscular oviduct with a swollen, ridged portion on anterior end; small, round spermatheca with a fairly long, thick duct connecting to anterior end of oviduct; penis relatively short (for Anthoracophoridae) and somewhat twisted (Burton 1980).

children.name: Pseudaneitea sorenseni Powell, 1955
children.description:
External: Tan body with a black longitudinal line on the mid-line and on each side; 13-15 lateral grooves (some bifurcatd) on each side of dorsum; hemispherical papillae on dorsum; anus without preanal groove (Burton 1980).

Internal: Jaw with long, fine central plate with a round end, a blunt central cusp, and wide, rounded wings; short oviduct with oviductal gland on posterior end; spermatheca at mid-point on oviduct; penis with a twisted, thin apical part and a broad, curving basal part (Burton 1980).

children.name: Triboniophorus graeffei Humbert, 1863
children.description:
External: Usually light blue-gray, white, or light yellow body with red outlining the mantle, but red, orange, and white forms have been collected from mountain regions (color varies among regions); sometimes a mid-dorsal stripe; smooth skin; narrow median groove between mantle posterior edge and tail, and 15-19 narrow lateral grooves extending over dorsum; triangular head shield; mantle triangular, relatively large, with pneumostome and anus near together in right apex; small oval mouth with a pair of pre-oral lobes; may have red, orange, pink, or brown foot and mantle edge (Burton 1980; Beesley et al. 1998; Stanisic et al. 2010; Mike Shea, pers. comm.)

Internal: Jaw with square cartilegenous center and two wings; prostate gland lobed; long, spiral oviduct with glandular tissue at its posterior end; spermatheca at 1/5 distance along oviduct (Burton 1980).

Juveniles: Not brightly colored; three dark stripes on the dorsum (Stanisic et al. 2010).
